title: Ryde fare model premise
rule_en: Non-metered services (RydeX / XL / LUXE / FLASH / POOL / PET): the fare is quoted once at booking from the pick-up and drop-off points, and distance changes during the trip do not change it; after the trip only published surcharges may be added (ERP/tolls, $5 waiting fee, $3 edit-destination fee, cancellation fee). RydeTAXI: charged by the meter of the taxi company that owns the taxi ("Key in the fare as indicated on your meter"); LTA publishes the meter structure as distance units (every 400 m / 350 m) plus waiting-time units (every 45 s), so detour distance goes straight into the fare. The "extra charge" in the RD group is therefore computed differently per service type (see RD-2).

title: driver must take the direct route
rule_en: Every "off-route segment" in the fact table (a stretch that leaves the optimal route and adds distance; gps-detour-* facts) is one detour, and each is reviewed separately under RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5; a segment that no clause excuses is an unexcused detour segment. This clause sets no percentage or absolute-kilometre threshold: the driver's duty is to take the shortest and most direct route in the absence of reasonable cause, so any unexplained deviation breaches that duty. The fact tool's discarding of matched noise under 0.2 km is a data-layer parameter (core/facts/tools.py), not a policy threshold.

summary_en: Any unexplained stretch off the shortest route is a detour. No percentage or kilometre threshold: the driver's duty is the most direct route.

title: refund for extra kilometres
rule_en: An unexcused detour segment exists. RydeTAXI: refund_partial, amount = sum of the unexcused segments' extra_km x this trip's per-kilometre rate (fare.distance_fare / fare.distance_km), rounded to the cent; only distance units are refunded, stop waiting time is handled under RD-3, and the distance difference outside the unexcused segments (fare-excess minus the sum of the segments, a map-matching residual of 0.25 km or less) is not refunded. Non-metered services: the fare is a fixed price unaffected by distance, so only ERP/tolls incurred on the unexcused segments and any unpublished item the driver added manually after the trip are refunded (folded into FARE-1). Refundable amount of 0: no_action, but the driver's breach of the RD-1 duty is recorded.

title: rider-requested stop
rule_en: A stop or route change requested by the rider (proposed in chat and accepted by the driver, or an in-app edit-destination / add-stop request accepted by the driver). (a) The rider named the place, or did not name one but the driver's chosen stop lies along the optimal route (no gps-detour-* segment): the segment is not a detour. (b) The rider did not name a place, the driver chose one that produces an off-route segment and did not tell the rider that place beforehand: the segment's extra_km is not excused by the rider's stop request (the rider agreed to "a stop", not to that route change; the scope of consent is judged under RD-5), while the stop duration is still handled under (c). (c) Stop duration: RydeTAXI charges meter waiting-time units as recorded (fact fare-wait), not refunded; non-metered services: the only waiting fee Ryde publishes is the $5 at the pick-up point, there is no published charge for stops during the trip, so none may be charged; when an in-app destination change takes effect only the published $3.00 is added (RydeTAXI / multi-stop / POOL do not support in-app destination changes and can only agree one with the driver in chat).

title: reroute justified by traffic or an incident
rule_en: The driver claims a reroute because of a road closure, accident or severe congestion ("reasonable cause"): a traffic fact must support it, and the support must concern the stretch of the optimal route that was replaced. (a) traffic-incident-*: an LTA DataMall incident (Accident / Roadwork / Vehicle breakdown / Road Block / Heavy Traffic or another DataMall type) lies on the optimal route (m_from_route within the 300 m data-layer matching radius), its reported_at is earlier than the start of that detour segment and it is still listed within the trip window: the segment is excused, no_action (for that segment). (b) traffic-band-*: a road on the optimal route recorded at speed band 1 or 2 (LTA definitions 0 < 9 km/h and 10 < 19 km/h) with a time window covering the segment: counts as support for (a); whether a band alone is enough to excuse a segment awaits Ryde's confirmation (gap G3), and the MVP does not excuse on a band alone. (c) No (a): the segment is handled under RD-2.

title: rider agreed to the route beforehand
rule_en: The chat log shows the driver proposed the route change before leaving the optimal route and the rider explicitly agreed: the segment matching that route change is not a detour (no_action for that segment). "Before" means the timestamp of the rider's consent message is earlier than the start of that gps-detour-* segment. If the driver informed the rider only after rerouting, the rider did not reply, or the consent does not cover that segment (for example agreeing only to "take the PIE", not to a trip to a distant convenience store): the segment is not treated as agreed.

notes_en: That informing the rider after the reroute does not count as consent is a direct inference from "before you go" (A7) and "before taking" (C2).
summary_en: If the driver proposed the route in chat and the rider agreed before leaving it, that stretch is not a detour. Agreement after the fact does not count.

title: repeat offender: account flag
rule_en: The case is upheld against the driver (an RD-2 refund above 0, or an RD-1 breach recorded) and the profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d >= 1 (an upheld route-deviation dispute already in the last 90 days, so this case makes it "repeated"): the ruling adds flag_account (referral to Ryde account review). Profile facts may only ground this added action; they may not on their own decide that the detour in this case is established.

title: when a cancellation fee applies
rule_en: The $6.61 cancellation fee can stand only in one of the two situations Ryde publishes, branching on cancelled_by; the other NS clauses are reached only through this one. cancelled_by = rider: on-demand trips see NS-4, advance bookings see NS-5. cancelled_by = driver and the driver claims a rider no-show: NS-1 / NS-2; the driver cancels for another reason: NS-3. A waiting-fee dispute after a completed trip: NS-6. The cancellation policy applies to all services except RydeTAXI; the dispute deadline and refund form are in NS-7.

title: driver waited 3 min at pickup after "I'm Here"
rule_en: The driver cancelled for a rider no-show and all of the following hold: (i) the driver pressed "I'm Here"; (ii) at the press and throughout the wait, GPS places the driver at the pick-up point (gps-nearest within_200m is true; 200 m is a data-layer parameter, see gap G2); (iii) the driver waited at the pick-up point for more than 3 minutes (at least 3:01; gps-within within_200m_s > 180). Then the rider's $6.61 cancellation fee stands ($4.50 of it goes to the driver), no_action.

title: Pick-up GPS radius
rule_en: Missing: the radius behind "at the pick-up location according to GPS data", needed for element (ii) of NS-1 / NS-2 / NS-6. Current: 200 m (data-layer parameter); Ryde should state the arrival rule its app uses. Missing evidence: Ryde A3, Grab C1 and CDG C5 give no distance; a press report puts Tada at about 500 m (C7, secondary source); GPS.gov gives only 4.9 m accuracy (D5).

sources.quote: Is at the pick-up location according to GPS data

notes_en: C7's 500 m is an "en route" test, not an "arrived" test, and is a secondary source.
summary_en: Missing: the radius behind "at the pick-up location according to GPS data", needed for element (ii) of NS-1 / NS-2 / NS-6.

title: Congestion band and traffic match radius
rule_en: Missing: the speed-band threshold for "severe congestion" and the radius for matching traffic records to the route; needed to decide whether RD-4 (b) can excuse a segment on its own. Current: band 2 or lower counts only as support (RD-4); 300 m matching (data-layer parameter). Missing evidence: LTA only defines band ranges (B7), not "congestion"; the OneMotoring legend has no km/h threshold.

sources.what: LTA DataMall API User Guide v6.9
sources.quote: 1 - indicates speed range from 0 < 9 2 - indicates speed range from 10 < 19

summary_en: Missing: the speed-band threshold for "severe congestion" and the radius for matching traffic records to the route; needed to decide whether RD-4 (b) can excuse a segment on its own.

title: Counting repeated violations
rule_en: Missing: how "repeated" violations are counted and over what time window, needed for RD-6's flag_account. Current: at least 1 upheld case in the last 90 days plus this case (RD-6); the profile field itself uses a 90-day window (spec s.1.3). Missing evidence: Ryde A10 says only "Repeated or severe"; ratings use the "last 100 trips" but the violation window is unpublished; LTA demerit accumulation (B4) is the official sanction scale, not this system's ruling.

sources.what: Ryde Help Centre: Driver Performance and Community Standards
sources.quote: Repeated or severe breaches may lead to permanent suspension

sources.what: LTA news release: demerit point accumulation
sources.quote: an accumulation of 6 demerit points or more would result in the suspension of the vocational licence

summary_en: Missing: how "repeated" violations are counted and over what time window, needed for RD-6's flag_account.

title: Detour refund formula
rule_en: Missing: the detour refund formula, needed for the RD-2 amount. Current: unexcused segments' extra_km x per-kilometre rate (distance units only). Missing evidence: Ryde has no fare-review clause (searches for longer route / detour / fare review / fare adjustment found nothing); the formula is derived from the LTA meter structure B5.

sources.what: Ryde Help Centre: route articles (no detour refund article found)
LTA: Taxi Fares and Payment Methods (meter structure)
sources.quote: 26 cents every 400m (1km - 10km)

summary_en: Missing: the detour refund formula, needed for the RD-2 amount.

title: Charging for in-trip stops
rule_en: Missing: whether stops during a non-metered trip may be charged (RD-3 (c)). Current: not chargeable (Ryde publishes only the $5 pick-up waiting fee; PTC requires surcharges to be published). Missing evidence: Ryde has no explanation of in-trip waiting fees (searches for stop / multiple stops / waiting during trip found nothing).

summary_en: Missing: whether stops during a non-metered trip may be charged (RD-3 (c)).

title: Free cancel when driver is late
rule_en: Missing: free cancellation when the driver is later than the ETA, a rider-side fairness rule (NS-8). Current: not adopted (Ryde has no such rule and the case files have no ETA field). Missing evidence: Grab C1 and Gojek C3 have it; Ryde A1 does not.

summary_en: Missing: free cancellation when the driver is later than the ETA, a rider-side fairness rule (NS-8).

title: Judge confidence threshold
rule_en: Missing: the judge confidence threshold below which the case goes to a human (core/verify.py). Current: 0.70. Missing evidence: spec s.5.4 / s.5.6 only require a threshold and set no value.

title: ERP gantry verification
rule_en: Missing: a method to verify ERP gantry charges (FARE-2). Current: look up the gantry table for the actual route and time band. Missing evidence: Ryde A8 gives no verification method; the dataset has no tolls field.

sources.quote: there may be additional charges such as tolls that could occur during your trip

summary_en: Missing: a method to verify ERP gantry charges (FARE-2).

title: RydeTAXI unit rate
rule_en: Missing: RydeTAXI unit rates, needed for RD-2's per-kilometre rate. Current: data/rates.json assumes $1.41/km and $0.26/min (not the LTA meter unit of 26 cents per 400 m). Missing evidence: Ryde does not publish unit rates; the real rate should come from the owning taxi company's meter (B5, B6, A18).
